what_matters.head: Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal, and Lumentum fell 18.6%, about 3.4 times its usual daily move.
what_matters.detail: When the deal closes, each Lumentum share becomes 4.5 Marvell shares, about $1,132 on the companies' figures, a 23.9% premium to Lumentum's 28 Oct close. Because the ratio is fixed, Lumentum now moves with Marvell, which closed at $171.41, down 13.2% (Motley Fool's quote). At that price 4.5 Marvell shares are worth about $771, so Lumentum closed about 11% below what the deal would pay. A gap like that usually reflects the chance the deal fails and the long wait: closing is expected in the first half of 2028, after both shareholder votes and regulators. Motley Fool pointed to the price tag and the dilution for Marvell holders. Lumentum also reported its quarter the same day, three days early (see Earnings).

what_matters.head: The chip fund fell another 3.8%, about 1.5 times its usual move, while about 7 in 10 S&P 500 stocks rose.
what_matters.detail: AMD fell 7.5%, about 2.1 times usual, before its results tomorrow at 05:05 SGT. Intel fell 8.8%, Sandisk 6.6% and Micron 5.8%. Yahoo Finance gave no single cause and counts about $3.7 trillion of value lost by chip and memory stocks since 6 Oct. By 12:05 SGT today SK Hynix was down 5.1% and Samsung 3.9%.

what_matters.head: US oil fell 7.2% to about $97 a barrel, about 2.7 times its usual daily move, on hopes of US–Iran peace talks.
what_matters.detail: Reuters reported that Iran's president said the Supreme Leader had given the government authority for peace talks, and that Qatari mediators flew to Tehran on Monday evening to discuss a possible US–Iran deal. Trump said Iran wants a deal and one could happen. Brent settled 7.6% lower at $104.77.

after_data.text: US officials told the Wall Street Journal that the US military struck Iran's Qeshm Island, in the Strait of Hormuz, on Monday. Officials called the strikes limited and defensive, after Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired at a US aircraft, and a US official told Fox News it was not the start of expanded strikes. Iran's foreign ministry said the strait could reopen within two days if the US lifts its naval blockade and ends hostilities. CNBC's report is timed 21:51 New York time on Monday, after the close, so it is not in Monday's US prices. At the 12:05 SGT run US oil was $96.66, close to Monday's $96.46 settlement.

recent.headline: Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal, and Lumentum fell 18.6%, about 3.4 times its usual daily move.
Intel fell 28.6% on Friday, about 7.5 times its usual daily move, and the chip fund fell 8.2%, about 3.5 times usual.
Alphabet fell 12.3% on Thursday, about 8 times its usual daily move, on volume 3.6 times normal. It was the first full session after its Q3 results.
Alphabet fell 9.8% in after-hours trading after its profit came in below forecasts. Microsoft rose 2.9% after hours on faster cloud growth. Neither move is in Wednesday's US prices.
SK Hynix's third-quarter revenue passed 100 trillion won for the first time, and operating profit beat forecasts. By 12:05 SGT its shares were up 10.5%, 2.2× their usual day.
